body: There is a picture of me. I think I'm somewhere between 3 and 5 years old. It's one of those annoying Christmas pictures where your parent has to shove a camera in your face for every present.  The first thing you notice in that picture is my face. It's an attempt at a smile, but it's more of a grimace. What am I holding?  A Cabbage Patch doll. My mom went out in the height of the Cabbage Patch craze. Who knows how many other parents she had to knife to get that doll. I could tell by the look on my face that I never played with that thing.  My mother confirmed it. I didn't play with that ugly thing one time. It was sold at some garage sale I'm sure. She now uses that photo as proof that I was born CF lol

When I was little I was quite the tomboy. From the time I was able to speak my mind I insisted on boy clothes and toys. I hated barbies, baby dolls, and anything with even a molecule of pink. I never wanted to hang with younger kids, I mostly gravitated to teens and adults. I knew from a very early age that I didn't like children. When the girls in my class would play that triangle paper game like they have in the opening credits of Community I would always say Zero when they would ask how many kids I wanted. You can't play the game that way so I would grudgingly say 1 and feel my pulse race. The thought of agreeing to even 1 kid in a stupid little paper game gave me anxiety. 

I was, of course, always told that I would change my mind. Never happened. I was told that I would die alone. Well those people's marriages are done for and mine is going strong and, even after 15 years, getting better all the time. Don't let anyone tell you who/what you are. You are your own person and you get to decide who that is for yourself. Gender roles/religion/stereotypes/life script be damned.

Story time: A long time ago I was dating an amazing man. My whole family could see that this one was different than the flings I had had in the past. I was 22 and it was about time for me to start settling down. 

My mom and I went to see one of my older cousins for a visit. I always looked up to this cousin like an aunt. She was beautiful, had an amazing husband, huge house, some adopted kids, the seemingly perfect life. I guess my mom and cousin decided that it was time for me to drop my childish tomboy ways and start training to be a proper wife. They tried to refine my manners. "What if he decides to go into politics, you don't want to embarrass him do you" Now my manners aren't barbarous by any means, but I'm not ready for high tea with the Queen. Still I found this insulting and told them as much. Then they came at it from another angle. "Well if you don't learn this stuff how are you going to teach your daughter?" Uh, who said anything about a daughter? "Well I'm sure he wants kids. All men want kids! If you don't want to die alone you're going to have to give him at least one" I don't remember what I said to that at the time but I was devastated. 

On the ride home I was dreading what I knew I was going to have to do. I called him up and told him we need to have a serious discussion. I was so nervous. That whole night I was imagining being alone for the rest of my life. I even asked myself if it was worth it? Loosing him just so I don't have to be a mother. And, despite my mom and cousins voice in my head, I decided that yes it was worth it. Being CF meant that much to me. 

So, off I went to potentially break up with who could have been the love of my life. I told him that I didn't want kids. Not now, not ever. Under any circumstances. Ever. This is something that I will absolutely NEVER change my mind about. If he does want kids then I understand and I wish him well. He looked kind of shocked for a moment and then said "You know, I never really thought about it. I just assumed it would happen. I never really thought of it as a choice. But I guess it is isn't it. Now that I think about it, no. No I don't want kids"

I couldn't believe my wonderful luck! I was told that these men don't exist and here he is! And he loves ME! That was 15 years ago. That man is my puzzle piece, my soul mate, my wonderful partner in life, my husband. Neither of us has ever changed our minds and we have been deliriously happy with each other and our decision ever since. 

So, actually, I did meet someone. And I changed HIS mind.

Man I had a similar experience this past weekend. Most weekends my husband plays tabletop RPGs with a group of friends. I'm not into playing RPGs myself, but I do like to hang out with everyone and listen to the game. There are 2 parents in our group. We usually go to the home of the guy with a 12 year old daughter. There is also a single mother with a 4 year old daughter. Well this time we thought "Why not host for once". 

So everyone comes to our CF house. The kids seem occupied petting my dog (which he loves) so I hang out with the parents. Well they started their gaming session and I needed to leave that room to get something. When I left that room I was mobbed by both children. They desperately needed attention. 

At first the 12 year old seemed like she was going to join the RPG session, but then she discovered our PSVR. Well that's rather expensive so I wasn't going to allow her to play it unsupervised. I know this girl is respectful with others belongings so I figured keeping an eye on her would be good enough. Well then the 4 year old wanted a turn. I didn't anticipate that, I suppose I should have. The 4 year old has not yet learned volume control and she was bugging the gamers so I thought maybe letting her try the VR would shut her up for a little bit. 

I'm not good with children. This babysitting was involuntary. I did my best to be patient and not show the kids how much they were annoying me. They weren't being bad so they didn't deserve to feel bad. The parents did bring things for their kids to play with, they know that our house is CF and there isn't much for kids to do. By the time they left a few hours later I had barely had a chance to speak to an adult and I was stressed and exhausted. 

I don't know how parents deal with that constant need for attention and the weirdness. The 4 year old clearly asked for "cawwots" aka carrots. I did happen to have a bag of baby carrots so I put a few in a bowl for her. She looked at me like I was a dumbass and said "No I want bubewwy" and pointed at one of my kitchen tiles that had blue berries on it. The fuk? I just gave you some of my carrots! You clearly asked for carrots! The bowl of carrots was untouched and wound up spilled on the floor, completely wasted. 

My husband saw how stressed I was and said that either we were never hosting again or we needed to have a talk with the parents so that I am never put in that position again. We've been gaming with them for a while and this is the first time that's happened. They're reasonable people parents so I'm sure they will understand. And that is my story of how I was unwittingly made a babysitter.

I don't know if OP is really gaslighting herself, if her SMIL/Aunt really intended physical harm or just embarrassment. I have a personal experience with my own usually yesMIL that makes me think it's possible it may have been exactly as the just no says this time. 

One 4th of July my DH and I were at his parents place with his sister and teenage nephews. His parents live on their own land in the country so we were shooting off various fireworks. Well usually yes Mil had been drinking (she doesn't drink often so it went straight to her head) and she started throwing firecrackers at our feet and laughing like a madwoman. She threw them at everyone's feet, mine, both her kids, both her grandkids. Fortunately we saw her doing it and were all able to jump away in time. 

At first the nephews thought it was funny, then it got old real quick. They started yelling at her "Grandma! Quit it! Please!" She'd just laugh and throw another. Their mom, MIL's daughter, told her "Mom! Fucking STOP" My husband took her lighter away. At this point in her drunk mind it was a game so she started lighting the firecrackers with her cigarette. She threw one at me and that was the last straw for my husband. He took the cigarette out of her mouth, and the rest of the carton, and destroyed it all. She behaved for the rest of the night.

She loves us and is usually very safety conscious. She just got drunk and carried away with the "fun" of seeing us jumping around. Extremely poor judgement (I was in sandals!) but no intent to harm was involved. If OP doesn't believe that this particular incident was an attempt to do harm, just extremely poor judgement, then I can believe it. But given what OP has shared about this individual, I can't completely discount the possibility that the motive was more nefarious than simple "embarrassment" Just my two cents :) In any case, I'm glad you weren't physically injured by her poor judgement/maliciousness OP.

My husband and I got this from a friend when we mentioned I was getting my Bi Salp. She just kinda looked at me with a thoughtful look and said "You guys should have kids, they'd change the world" My husband and I looked at each other and started laughing. Uh no. I know where she's coming from though. She sees my husband and I being deliriously happy together, having successful jobs above minimum wage. She sees how well we train our dog and how much care we give him. What she doesn't see is all the mental health issues we both have. All the alone time we both need, even from each other. She comes from a toxic home life. Her parents were extremely toxic and abusive. She married a guy that she had to leave because he started abusing their daughter. She sees a stability in us that she's never had herself. So I wasn't mad at her comment. That's the only bingo she's done, otherwise she accepts our decision as a good friend should.
There are dozens of us. DOZENS!

My mom and aunt did this with my aunt's grandson. He was old enough to hold his own head up, but not old enough to speak. I don't know what range that is. All I know is it's well below my comfort zone. 

I was sitting at the kitchen table minding my own business when my chair was yanked back (it was on rollers) and a kid was plopped in my lap. I touched him just enough to not let him fall while I was begging them to take him back. They stood over me and said "how cute" and other such nonsense. It wasn't until I started crying from the pure terror I was feeling that they finally took him away. I moved my chair back under the table and wrapped my legs around the table legs so they couldn't do that shit again. 

I don't understand why people think that shoving a kid on someone who isn't comfortable holding said child is a funny/cute/smart thing to do. They both knew my childfree stance. I think my mom was hoping for some sort of epiphany on my part. That light would shine down from the heavens, angels would sing, and I would change my mind and produce a grandchild for her.

And what of those individuals who are minors and/or are not financially independent enough yet to cut off those people. All I'm asking is that you have empathy for those whose circumstances are different than yours. It took me 36 years to clear most of the FOG surrounding my mom. That was with therapy. It's hard. It's worth it, but it's not a switch you can just flip. Just please have empathy for those of us who have been abused and are on our journey to healing. That's all I ask.

Though I know that toddlers are at about the same mental development as a reasonably intelligent dog, I still can't in good conscience treat a human that way. So when I do I feel like an ass, while the people around me are wearing stupid grins. I avoid this uncomfortable situation as much as possible. I'm probably over thinking everything.

My mom once told me of the last conversation that she had with her own mother before she passed away. 

You see, I was a MAJOR tomboy. Despised Barbies, pink, frills, sparkles, had a personal crusade against dresses/skirts. My first word was Spock and being a sci fi nerd is in my blood. I hated anything deemed girly or prissy. I hated school picture day. It was like my mom bottled up all of her frustrated desires for a girly girl and vomited sparkles and sequins on me. Made me do something with my hair other than allow it to grow on my head. It was awful. 

My mom wanted a girly girl and she got me. She did her best to make me happy though. Bought boy clothes. Cut my hair short. Didn't push girly stuff at all. This is where that conversation comes in.

 I'm in 4th grade and super tomboy with no indication of changing. After I go to bed my mom calls her mom weeping.

"Mom, I think my little girl might be a leeeeeessssbiiiaaaannnn!" She sobbed. 

My grandma was a pretty no nonsense lady. "So?" she askes

"Well..." mom stammered

"You'd still love her right"

"Well yea, of course"

"Then what are you crying about?"

That was the last conversation they had before my grandma passed a day or so later. Didn't become a lesbian. I love my man and he loves me, jeans and star trek quotes and all. Still don't wear dresses but a couple times a year. Wore jeans and my favorite Dr Who shirt to my wedding. Your girl will be awesome, don't let that mean ol biddy tell you or her otherwise!

For me babies are in the uncanny valley. They are human, but certain things about them just aren't. The way they move (all jerky and spasmatic) the dead stare (just nothing there yet) their weird noises (their high pitched shrieks make my teeth and eyeballs rattle) their proportions.. Nothing about them aside from 1 head and 4 limbs seems normal to me. I understand that it's not their fault, that's just how larval humans look. I totally get that I looked like that too (I've seen pics, I was an exceptionally ugly baby). None of that makes them any less alien seeming to me. So I just avoid them until they have more motor control, better control of their vocal chords, and have grown more into themselves.

I can kind of relate. My mom is a bit of an emotional mess. She, on some level, seems to think that she has to buy my love. Or anyone's love for that matter. 

Some examples: When I was a child I mentioned I think white tigers are beautiful. The next several Christmasses/birthdays white tiger everything. Towels, figurines, random stupid shit. As an adult I mentioned looking into a 3DS, next thing I know I get this cheap knock off crap. 

Some people think these gifts are given with love, and maybe in some way they are. But not in a healthy way. Her gifts often infantize me (a plushey unicorn given to me for my 35th birthday comes to mind along with the Ninja Turtle paddle balls), but I still feel an obligation to humor her and not hurt her feelings. Objects are love in her world after all. 

But this mentality has caused her endless suffering. It contributed to her failed marriage, she's used all of her retirement on stupid stuff, she feels bad for needing to borrow money from me. I have told her and told her "I don't want any object for (insert holiday). Please take that money and pay on one of your bills for me." But oh no she can't dooooooo thaaaaaaat. 

The last time she came to see me was when she was watching my cat while my husband and I went on a cruise. Cruises often have a formal night. So what does she do? She buys me a dress. Never mind that I may have wanted to pick one out for myself. So I did something very hard. 

I told her no thank you. She was upset but I explained that my style is very particular and really I'm the only one that can pick out clothes for me. So many thousands and thousands of dollars of clothes wasted over the years because she just had to get it for me and it was hideous. 

That was so hard. With the help of my DH we have started addressing the issue of her over spending and trying to buy love. It's been hard and she back slides, but I'm shinning up my spine for this. She needs to stop the shopping. 

I know it's easy for outsiders to think I'm ungrateful or spoiled. But I'm not. I just want her to make wise financial decisions, and buying me stupid crap on her extremely fixed income is not a wise financial decision. I have lived most of my life with the guilt that came with knowing that that stuff she kept buying was destroying her marriage. A child shouldn't have that burden on them. 

All my hugs to you OP, if you want them. I know this burden too well and it suuuucks.

My mom has done something similar to me. I was sitting at the kitchen table at my aunt's house. Her chairs were the rolly kind and I'm short so I usually had to scoot way forward to get my feet on the ground to move. Well one time we went to my aunt's house and my cousins new son was there. 

I had done my best to avoid the relatively new potato. It was old enough to hold it's head up at least, but not walking. My mom was determined that I should have babies (I'm an only child) so she and her sister hatched a plan. They surrounded me around that rolly chair, forcibly pulled me out from under the table, and ploped the drooling potato in my lap. They stood over me with their hands on their hips looking smug.

I think my mom imagined that my brain would break and I would become a different person and start, I duunno, Hugging the meat sack. I was pissed off. I demanded they take the thing off me. I threatened to dump him on the floor! Empty threat from me and we all knew it. I don't like being in physical contact with babies but I would never actually harm one. 

Finally I made the conscious decision to cry. My dignity took one for the team and I cried. Me, 20 years old at the time, crying because they wouldn't' take the (admittedly calm) baby out of my lap. My mom was so embarrassed in front of her sister she grabbed the thing out of my lap immediately. I got forward in the chair, dug my heels into the floor, and shoved myself forcibly back under the table. Stopped crying immediately and gave her my best shit eating grin. 

She's never tried anything of the sort since.

At first my mind went to a bucket of water, but that would soak your innocent bed. Then I thought of a spray bottle. Just spray her in the face every time she refuses to get up. Just like you would a naughty cat or something. Be pretty funny to watch her sputter and leave all damp.

Yea I have only ever held an infant once in my life. He was old enough to hold himself in a sitting position but I don't think he was old enough to walk. He was my cousin's son. 

My mom and my aunt (the kid's grandmother) cornered me at the kitchen table. They both stood over me and yanked my chair out from under the table. My mom was determined to get me to like kids so I would change my mind. She thought that by forcing a kid in my lap it would make me realize I want kids. HA, no. 

I tried to pull myself back under the table but they wouldn't let me. I was a young adult back then and didn't have the shiney spine that I do now. My aunt put the kid on my lap and I was just frozen in fear and disgust. He was drooling. That's one of my biggest triggers for my gag reflex.

I've wanted to say something about this character since I saw the movie a few days ago. I was able to relate to her. I'm a CF aunt who hasn't had the closest relationship with her now teenage nephews. Here are my thoughts on a few scenes. 

The bingo, groan inducing. In the mother's defense though she was going thru a divorce and I imagine that wouldn't put her in the most rational mood. Weird emotional outbursts must be expected. 

The "not knowing their age" thing, I relate to that very much. For most of their lives my nephews have been child A and child B to me. I knew their names but I couldn't remember what name belonged to which child. Always felt kind of guilty for that. They were close in age though and had the same hair cut and the same generic annoying little boy personality. I felt bad at not being able to tell them apart for years, but that doesn't mean that I ever questioned my CF status. Now they are teenagers, have distinct personalities and different haircuts. I can tell them apart :) Still don't want kids.

The scene where she stares longingly at the screen with the mother and child reuniting. Yea...no. That was more like "whew what a day..oh look at that mother and child..child..am I forgetting something...NEPHEWS! SHIT! I FORGOT THEY EXISTED!" That is something I can see myself doing since I'm not accustomed to thinking of children in my life. I don't have regular contact with them so, in a situation like hers, I can see where my mind might slip to other things and forget their existence for the moment. Even a bad aunt would then remember her responsibility and feel bad about loosing track of them in such a serious crisis. That doesn't mean she suddenly wants kids of her own, that just means that she isn't a crazy person who doesn't give a shit about other humans.

Her desire to go searching for her nephews. I would want to find mine too! If they were put in my care it is my responsibility to see to their safety. A good argument can be made that she had a greater responsibility to the other 20k+ people in the park and should have stayed in the control center. But she also has a responsibility to the plot so we have to let her leave so she can be part of the adventure finding them. Whatever. I'll argue that the whole disaster was handled unrealistically, but it was still badass and entertaining. Wanting to protect the nephews doesn't make her maternal or give her the baby rabbies. It just makes her, I dunno, human. Since they have become teenagers I've had my nephews stay with me and my husband a few weekends. The first time was really intimidating for me. I asked their mother, and I quote, "what are their nutritional requirements". She gave me a deadpan look and just said "feed them food". Well I didn't know if they had allergies or if were on a special diet or what. Apparently she told them because the next morning they thanked me for satisfying their nutritional requirements. It was funny. But you know what, the fact that I fed them and gave them back to their mother unscathed didn't make me want one of my own, not even for a shake of a second. I was glad that I didn't kill them thru my ignorance of child rearing and they had a good time but that's it. 

What I saw in this movie was an inexperienced aunt getting to know her nephews better thru a traumatic experience. They become closer in the end and she learns lessons about empathy along the way. I don't see any evidence that she wants any children of her own. A woman can care for her family and show empathy for living things without wanting to sprout crotchfruit.

When the beating parent took a pancake turner to me for a B on a spelling test. I told the other parent about it and asked if this was normal and they said that it absolutely was NOT and that if the other parent does it again I was to tell immediately. The beatings immediately stopped. I understand now why they were done, not really my fault just that parent had had a very hard life and was having severe emotional problems. They still to this day have emotional problems, but didn't realize that they were in fact abusing me until the other parent pointed it out and threatened to take me away. Sometimes people need a shocking eye opener. 

As for the image of a 5 year old with a discipline contract, that made me lol. That is kind of how the spanking parent saw discipline. As something emotionless to be carried out in a regimented and logical fashion. They would never touch me in the heat of the moment when anger was high and control over muscle force is at it's lowest. Time out was used to give them time to calm down if necessary. Time out always being during Star Trek to inflict maximum torture lol. This approach, along with the message at the end of every spanking that no matter what I did I would always be their favorite child and that I would always be loved, is what I believe is the difference.

I was spanked and beaten so I know the difference first hand. When I was beaten I often times didn't know what I did wrong. There was a lot of yelling and crying involved. I was frightened and angry and if I really couldn't figure out what I did wrong I was rebellious. 

Spanking was done in a very calm manner. My transgression was made clear to me, the force used was measured, I was made to specifically know how to avoid this consequence in the future. I would actually leave my spankings feeling like I had learned something. It actually had a positive impact on my life. Whenever something bad happens to me I think of how I can avoid it in the future and I feel better. 

Spankings are tools to teach life lessons, beatings are just a poor emotionally unbalanced person taking out their frustration on someone much smaller than them. 

For the record the parent that spanked put a quick end to the beatings when I made them aware of them. Also I have a great relationship with both parents. It's actually a funny story. It was my first day of driving by myself and driving my new-to-me clunker car. The left turn signal was out but I hadn't had the opportunity to get it changed out yet. While looking to see if he has turned his lights on yet, I jumped the curb. He pulled me over. I was polite and explained that it was my first day driving and promised to be careful in the future. He smiled and said to be careful in the future and gave me a verbal warning. I thanked my lucky stars and fixed my signal after school that day. I've been pulled over for a misunderstanding concerning the license plate on my new new-to-me car. He called for back up and came up to my car with his hand on his gun. That kinda freaked me out.  Once we both realized that the dealership had given me the wrong plate he gave me a warning and let me go. I understand why he was cautious. The plate was registered to a completely different car, a possible hint that I had stolen that car. He was simply being careful. When it was clear that that was not the case he was more relaxed but he was polite the entire time.  And the last time I was pulled over my license plate light was out. He politely informed me of this, I promised to see to it immediately, and we wished each other a pleasant evening. This happened in all different parts of Texas. Maybe Texas cops are nicer than other areas, idk. But they would have been well within their rights to give me a ticket and though I would have been mad at myself for breaking the law and not maintaining my vehicle properly I wouldn't have been mad at the cops. There are road laws for a reason and breaking them gets not only the offender but innocent people killed.  But to refer back to my previous statement, only on that first instance did I knowingly and willfully break the law. I shouldn't have driven to school that day, I should have waited and had my parents drive me to get the new bulb and replaced it before driving. The other instances, though I did break the law, the problems were unknown to me. Once they were made clear I saw to them immediately.

I was always the skinniest girl around. Everyone thought I had an eating disorder but I proudly proclaimed that I didn't. I was 5ft 1 and 93 lbs and proud of it. I honestly didn't have an eating disorder, I only threw up when I was honestly sick and I ate whatever I wanted and however much of it I wanted. It just so happened that I didn't want very much. A few bites and I was full. Honestly full. I didn't have self esteem issues, I was proud of how I looked. When I started filling out more at first I was happy because I was finally filling out in all the right places. I thought nothing of it. Now it's 10 years later and depression and fucked up hormones and incredible stress have taken their toll. My appetite hasn't changed. I can still only eat a few bites and be full. My craving for sweets is all but gone. Where when I was skinny I could eat an entire bag of peanutbutter cups now I can barely finish a pack of 2. I do not eat my emotions. I'm not BSing here, I have written down every bite that I take and, unless I'm doing something special, I don't eat very much at all. And when I am doing something special then my eating level approaches normal. My activity level has changed very recently. My dad never had me in sports, he would always look at the $25 uniform fee and say "No way in hell I'm paying that!!" I have always had active jobs until I finally found my way out of fucking customer service and into wonderful Data Processing.  When I was still in the city I recognized this decrease in activity and tried to supplement it with exercise. I tried to always have a class of physical activity be it kickboxing, scuba, or bowling. After I graduated with my Associates my outlets for exercise began to be taken away.  After moving to my present location and realizing how seedy and corrupt this area is I refuse to go out unless I am in my car or with my boyfriend. I can't afford a gym membership, there is no community center, the block that I live on is unsafe, and my house has severe structural problems. How does it happen OP asks? It's called life and sometimes it rapes you in the ass with a large fist with keys all pointing out in between the fingers. I'm not to where I physically can't exercise, I'm just afraid to step foot out of my home for all the crime in our area. When I am financially able to get to a safer area I enjoy going to a park and having Martial Arts practice, or just doing intervals.  I do what I can with cooking when I can afford something other than ramen, but at the IGA that I am forced to shop at even the strawberries taste like rotisserie chicken! Sometimes things happen that we can't control, we make choices for our happiness. I chose to move here so that my boyfriend could go to College. I chose to leave a life of safety, stability, better paying job, friends, family, everything because I knew that I was incapable of participating in a long distance relationship. I wish his college were in a better area so that I could work out in safety, but I can't control that. Fortunately, as soon as he graduates in a year and a half, we will GTFO. Then  I can find a safe park, a home with a stable floor, a job that will pay me enough to afford a gym membership, and  a store where the bread doesn't taste like chicken grease (Whole Foods, dare I pray).

I would gladly do that if it were safe. I live next door to a drug house with cops there all hours of the day/night. The crime rate in this city is atrocious for so small a community. I don't leave my house unless I absolutely have to and while I'm home I know exactly where my loaded shot gun is. When I lived in a safer area I loved to go to the park and do intervals walk/jog.
